goal.objective: After the user switches to Build mode, fix all nine confirmed review findings in /home/james/repos/computer-use: (1) prevent reading/deleting a user's screenshot through false capture ownership, including staggered and concurrent captures; (2) enforce OpenCode permissions before GUI mutations and other protected desktop operations; (3) report screenshot cleanup failures truthfully; (4) reject incomplete/corrupt PNGs before attaching them; (5) enforce the screenshot byte limit during reading, not after unbounded allocation; (6) account for screenshots that may be produced despite trigger failure, timeout, or cancellation; (7) make desktop_tree's schema match its implemented arguments; (8) preserve ambiguity candidates alongside backend errors; and (9) make handoff/resume goal recovery source-session-aware so it cannot substitute an unrelated goal. Preserve normal OpenCode behavior, existing desktop capabilities and safety boundaries, /handoff_resume naming, mandatory handoff plan/history, unrelated dirty and staged work, the goal plugin, MCP settings, and the current Code Mode configuration. Add regression coverage, reconcile documentation, and independently verify the real outcomes. Do not commit, push, publish a PR, deploy runtime copies, change security settings, or adopt a screenshot approach that changes user interaction without separate explicit approval.

plan.summary: Fix the nine confirmed review defects; safely reconcile the current open PRs with preserved local work; add automatic repo-local goal exports under docs/goals/<goal-id>/, a detailed plain-English planning skill, and /handoff creation/seeding/opening of a fresh same-worktree session. Leave upstream goal-plugin storage/behavior, MCPs and Code Mode unchanged. Integration uses isolated, reviewed, pinned revisions and preserves staged, unstaged and untracked work. Plan only until Build mode and explicit goal resumption.
completionCriteria: Finding 1: successful captures have demonstrable request-specific ownership; staggered user screenshots and concurrent requests cannot cause unrelated images to be read, attached, or deleted. A timing delay or filename difference alone is not accepted as ownership proof; successful native capture must still work.

Finding 2: desktop permission checks precede protected side effects and respect allow/ask/deny, with denials reaching the caller rather than being swallowed; tokens remain target-freshness guards, not authorization. Verify denied operations never reach the backend.

Finding 3: cleanup success is verified and cleanup failures return accurate retained-file/error information; no outcome or documentation falsely claims deletion or that an attachment is the only copy.

Finding 4: complete genuine PNG fixtures succeed, while truncated headers, incomplete image data, malformed chunks, and corrupt images are rejected before attachment; deletion still requires proven capture ownership.

Finding 5: file reads enforce a fixed byte budget before unbounded allocation, including files that grow while being read; oversize captures are refused and handled according to verified ownership and cleanup status.

Finding 6: trigger errors, timeouts, cancellation, and post-trigger failures have bounded lifecycle handling; possible or confirmed retained captures are reported accurately, and no unowned file is removed. Cancellation reaches trigger, wait/poll, and read operations as applicable.
Finding 7: every desktop_tree schema argument is implemented or removed; unsupported filters cannot silently become an unfiltered tree dump. Adapter and schema regression tests agree.

Finding 8: backend failure results retain useful stdout candidate summaries alongside stderr explanations, within the existing output budget; ambiguity continues to refuse mutation and supports a subsequent explicit nth selection.

Finding 9: handoffs preserve source project/directory, session and goal identity where available, goal status, plan and historical documentation. Resume never replaces that source with an unrelated current-session goal; missing or inaccessible source data has an explicit safe fallback. /handoff_resume remains the command name.

All nine findings have independently checked regression evidence; focused tests, health checks, whitespace/syntax checks, permission integration checks and an approved fresh-session screenshot interpretation test pass. The goal plugin, MCP configuration, codemode:false setting, security boundaries, unrelated dirty/staged work and standard coding tools remain unchanged; no unapproved commit, push, PR publication or runtime deployment occurs.
